item.title: Stablecoin supply posts largest 30-day drop since June 2022 – Link Glassnode dat
item.description:
Stablecoin supply posts largest 30-day drop since June 2022 – Link

Glassnode data shows major stablecoin supply fell by about $14.2B over the 30 days to November 9, the sharpest contraction since mid-2022. USDT also trades slightly below its $1 peg.

Capital appears to be exiting crypto for USD rather than rotating within the market, reducing liquidity for a near-term rebound.

On-chain monitoring showed BlackRock transferred 4,189 BTC (≈$305M) and 68,230 ETH (≈$139M) from ETF custody wallets to Coinbase Prime within a 30-minute window.

Large custodial transfers to exchange-linked prime brokerage accounts can precede more ETF redemptions or rebalancing.

item.title: OKX and NYSE parent ICE set Nov. 23 launch for tokenized securities venue, but m
item.description:
OKX and NYSE parent ICE set Nov. 23 launch for tokenized securities venue, but major Big Tech names opt out – Link

OKX and Intercontinental Exchange's joint venture OKXICE confirmed 70 tokenized assets, including Coinbase, Circle, and Robinhood, for a Nov. 23 launch under the SEC's innovation exemption framework. But 67 companies, including Meta, Tesla, Netflix, and Costco, have opted out, and Nasdaq has opposed the framework.

It shows a split path for tokenized equities, with crypto-native issuers embracing it while blue chips resist.

item.title: Avalanche rallies after NYSE selects its tech for tokenized securities clearing
item.description:
Avalanche rallies after NYSE selects its tech for tokenized securities clearing infrastructure – Link

Ava Labs said Avalanche will power the ledger infrastructure for an NYSE-affiliated clearinghouse supporting 24/7 trading and atomic settlement of tokenized equities. AVAX gained roughly 2% over the past 24h, with a sharper ≈10% move reported in the prior session.

This is a concrete institutional infrastructure win for AVAX as a settlement layer.

item.title: MARA sells ≈14,000 BTC ($1.1B) to repay debt and fund AI infrastructure – Link B
item.description:
MARA sells ≈14,000 BTC ($1.1B) to repay debt and fund AI infrastructure – Link

Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings sold 13,597 BTC, about 40% of its holdings, at an average price of $81,039. It used $750M of proceeds to fully repay Bitcoin-collateralized loans from Coinbase Credit and Two Prime, and has cut total debt by $1.4B since the start of 2026.

Continued miner selling into AI pivots could add incremental BTC supply pressure.

item.title: Initia l1 halted after $3.27M exploit via leaked cloud credentials – Link Initia
item.description:
Initia l1 halted after $3.27M exploit via leaked cloud credentials – Link

Initia suspended its Layer-1 network on Nov 10 after attackers used leaked GCP keys to forge IBC withdrawal proofs. The exploit drained roughly $3.27M in assets from escrow accounts, with another ≈$2.16M stuck on the halted chain.

The incident highlights how cloud-key security remains a major attack vector for L1s and could weigh on confidence until recovery is complete.

item.title: Jupiter launches four new products: baskets, vaults, portfolio V3, and revamped
item.description:
Jupiter launches four new products: baskets, vaults, portfolio V3, and revamped pulse – Link

Solana's largest trading platform rolled out a suite of new products on Nov 10–11, expanding beyond a pure DEX aggregator into a broader asset-management platform.

• Baskets: single-asset deposits into diversified token baskets
• Vaults: curator-managed yield strategies for stablecoins and RWAs, live in private beta
• Portfolio V3: upgraded interface with cross-chain transfers
• Pulse: revamped

The launch broadens Jupiter's product scope and could support JUP ecosystem engagement and TVL if adoption follows through.

item.description:
Goldman Sachs, Citi, and other major banks commit $270M to dollar stablecoin venture project faro – Link

Institutions including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander, and Deutsche Bank have committed roughly $270 million to fund five years of operations for Project Faro, a bank-led dollar stablecoin targeting a launch in H1 2027, with a euro stablecoin to follow.

The move shows growing traditional-finance commitment to stablecoins, but the launch is still over a year away and carries execution risk.

item.description:
Coinbase receives full national trust bank charter from the OCC – Link

The OCC elevated Coinbase's trust status from conditional to a full national trust bank charter. This formalizes Coinbase's place in the US banking regulatory framework and may support broader institutional use for custody and asset management.

A full charter can strengthen institutional trust in Coinbase's services and deepen its role in traditional finance infrastructure.

item.title: NYSE selects Avalanche for tokenized securities clearing infrastructure – Link A
item.description:
NYSE selects Avalanche for tokenized securities clearing infrastructure – Link

Avalanche will provide the core blockchain ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting NYSE's upcoming tokenized stock trading platform. The setup is meant to enable 24/7 trading, clearing, and atomic settlement of tokenized equities.

This is one of the most significant TradFi-to-blockchain integrations disclosed this year and points to growing willingness to use public blockchain rails for regulated securities.

item.title: Zcash developers propose cutting block interval to 20 seconds just days after NU
item.description:
Zcash developers propose cutting block interval to 20 seconds just days after NU7 upgrade – Link

Zcash developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft ZIP to reduce the target block interval from 25 to 20 seconds for the upcoming NU7.1 upgrade. The recent NU7 upgrade had already cut block times from 75 to 25 seconds.

Faster confirmations could improve ZEC's usability for payments and exchange settlement, even though price action has not yet reflected the protocol news.

item.title: AcryptoS DeFi protocol hacked for ≈$665,000, shuts down operations – Link The De
item.description:
AcryptoS DeFi protocol hacked for ≈$665,000, shuts down operations – Link

The DeFi yield aggregator ACryptoS disclosed a treasury exploit caused by a lack of input validation. Attackers were able to mint a majority of shares in 77 treasuries across 5 chains with minimal deposits. The team disabled deposits, kept withdrawals open, offered a 10% bounty, and said the project is ceasing operations.

Even established-looking DeFi protocols can still carry ongoing smart-contract risk.

item.title: THORChain and Wasabi wallet processed stolen Binance hack funds despite FBI appe
item.description:
THORChain and Wasabi wallet processed stolen Binance hack funds despite FBI appeal – Link

The Wall Street Journal reported that after the recent Binance-linked theft, hackers laundered funds across 10,000+ wallets. THORChain reportedly processed over $46M of stolen funds within 72 hours and collected over $200K in fees, while nearly $4M moved through Wasabi Wallet despite law-enforcement requests to stop processing.

This adds compliance and reputational risk for decentralized infrastructure used in illicit fund flows.

item.description:
Binance hack fallout widens as Fed and OCC begin checking US banks for spillover risk – Link

Following last week's $6.3B Binance security breach, the Federal Reserve and OCC started contacting banks to check for unusual activity or vulnerabilities that could be exploited by similar attack methods.

Regulators appear to be treating the hack as a systemic-risk issue, which could raise scrutiny on exchange security and crypto-bank linkages.

item.title: Chainalysis says Binance hack funds are being laundered through Chinese networks
item.description:
Chainalysis says Binance hack funds are being laundered through Chinese networks – Link

Chainalysis reported that hackers behind the $6.3B Binance theft are routing part of the stolen funds through Chinese money-laundering networks. Earlier reports said Tether and Circle had frozen roughly $823M in stolen USDT/USDC within an hour of the exploit.

The recovery effort is becoming more complex and multi-jurisdictional, keeping pressure on exchange security and stablecoin freeze protocols.

item.title: AI-stock meltdown drags crypto into a $1B+ liquidation cascade – Link The Nasdaq
item.description:
AI-stock meltdown drags crypto into a $1B+ liquidation cascade – Link

The Nasdaq 100 had its worst session since 2020, with AI/chip stocks sliding hard — Nvidia ~-9%, Micron ~-17% — while crypto-linked equities like MSTR, COIN, and CRCL fell 9–13%. Bitcoin dropped over 5% to near $75,600–$76,000, and total crypto liquidations hit about $1.08B, including ≈$954M in longs.

Crypto is still trading like a risk asset tied to tech/AI sentiment, so continued equity volatility could add more downside pressure.

item.title: Zcash activates NU7 upgrade, freezing ≈$16M in oldest privacy pool – Link Zcash'
item.description:
Zcash activates NU7 upgrade, freezing ≈$16M in oldest privacy pool – Link

Zcash's NU7 network upgrade went live, invalidating version-4 transactions and making roughly 12,224 ZEC (≈$15-16M) in the legacy "Sprout" privacy pool unspendable. It also cut block times to roughly a third of previous levels.

The upgrade is a major technical migration for a top-20 privacy coin and may affect throughput, fee dynamics, and legacy fund access.

item.description:
Base mainnet ships denim upgrade, cutting block time to 200ms – Link

Base's fourth independent network upgrade went live on mainnet, shortening block intervals to 200 milliseconds and disabling Flashblocks.

Faster block times can improve transaction finality on one of the largest L2s and support higher-frequency DeFi and trading activity.
